culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Kamakura City's public manners ordinance (in force April 2019) names nuisance behaviours it asks visitors to avoid: eating or drinking while walking in narrow or crowded places where you could soil someone's clothes; stopping in the roadway to take photos; photographing near railway tracks or other dangerous spots; leaving hiking paths; cutting or picking plants; using fire near grass on paths; running past walkers, or riding bikes and motorbikes, on narrow or crowded paths. It is a manners ordinance with no penalties, and it doesn't ban eating while walking.
culture-and-protocol.note: Kamakura only, from the city's ordinance page.

laws.rule: Kanagawa Youth Protection and Development Ordinance (神奈川県青少年保護育成条例), art. 24. The ordinance sets the late-night period as 11 pm to 4 am. A guardian may not let a young person (generally under 18) go out in that period except for special reasons. Anyone else is barred from taking such a young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in that period without the guardian's consent or another proper reason. The offence for others carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.
laws.heading: 神奈川県青少年保護育成条例 (Kanagawa), curfew for young people

laws.rule: Kanagawa's 神奈川県迷惑行為防止条例 (Kanagawa Nuisance Acts Prevention Ordinance), art. 9, bans pushy touting and soliciting (客引き, 誘引) and loitering to wait for customers (客待ち) in entertainment districts. Since 1 May 2025 it covers touting for sexual services regardless of the sex of either person, and street touting for izakaya and karaoke shops (no penalty for that last group). Police can order a person to stop; the prefectural public safety commission can order businesses to suspend operations. A further amendment takes effect on 1 September 2026 on location-tracking tags used without consent. Yen at A$1 = JPY 110.82 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).
laws.heading: 神奈川県迷惑行為防止条例 art. 9 (touting), amended 1 May 2025

laws.rule: Yokohama City’s parks bureau says smoking has been banned in city parks since April 2025. Its notice separately asks people not to smoke while walking.
laws.heading: No Smoking in Parks

laws.rule: Zushi City, Zushi beach, in the swimming-beach season (2026: 3 July to 6 September): drinking alcohol on the sand is banned, including alcohol you bring in; drinking is allowed only in the beach houses (umi no ie) on their licensed footprint. Basis: 逗子市「安全で快適な逗子海水浴場の確保に関する条例」(Zushi Ordinance on Securing a Safe and Comfortable Zushi Swimming Beach, 2014 No. 6), art. 5 para. 2 item 2 (drinking), with open-flame cooking in item 1. The city says the ban applies all day, not only in swimming hours (9 am to 5 pm). The mayor can warn and order a stop (art. 6), and the city says repeat offenders can be made to leave. No fine amount is published in the pages read.

Zushi City, Zushi beach, in the swimming-beach season: using speakers or public-address equipment to play sound or music is banned, and so is showing tattoos that make others uneasy or afraid (the city asks people to cover them with a towel or shirt). Basis: 逗子市「安全で快適な逗子海水浴場の確保に関する条例」art. 5 para. 2 items 3 and 4, and art. 6 (guidance, warning, stop order). The city list also bans rough behaviour, smoking inside the swimming area, vehicles on the sand, and, from 9 am to 5 pm, dogs, boards and powered craft inside the swimming area. The ordinance sets no fine.

Kamakura City, the three swimming beaches (Zaimokuza, Yuigahama, Koshigoe), in the swimming season (2025: 1 July to 31 August): drinking on the sand is banned. The city bulletin of July 2025 lists the beach manners as: no drinking on the sand, no exposed tattoos, no sound equipment, litter only in bins, smoking only at smoking spots, no barbecue or fire, no dangerous play gear, no animals in the swimming area. Basis: 鎌倉市海水浴場のマナーの向上に関する条例 (Kamakura Ordinance on Improving Swimming-Beach Manners), art. 6 and its schedule (別表), which the city proposed in 2014 to turn into prohibited acts with guidance, warnings and stop-or-leave orders. The current consolidated text was not read; the list is from the city bulletin.

Kamakura City, the swimming beaches in the season: playing music or sound through sound equipment is banned, and so is showing tattoos that frighten others (the 2014 wording). See the Kamakura beach-manners ordinance, art. 6 and schedule. Staff and guards patrol the beaches. Separately, the city bans rocket fireworks and similar loud fireworks on beaches, in parks and other places from 10 pm to 6 am, with extra patrols at Shichirigahama on summer weekends from 9 pm; the bulletin names a city ordinance but not its title.

Hakone Town: 箱根町をきれいにする条例 (Hakone Keep-the-Town-Clean Ordinance, in force 1 October 2001) applies to visitors (滞在者, defined in art. 2 item 5 to include tourists and people passing through). Art. 8 bans dumping waste on roads, rivers, lakes, parks or other people's land, leaving pet droppings, throwing fishing weights, hooks and line into rivers and lakes or near them, and defacing other people's buildings with graffiti. A person who ignores a mayor's order under this ordinance can face a court fine (art. 20 to 22) of up to JPY 20,000 (about A$180, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82) for ordinary breaches; higher caps of JPY 30,000 and JPY 50,000 apply to vending-machine duties.
